_note: 日本酒の産地の系譜。品目ハブ（/en/eat/sake/）の横並び表と、各系譜ページがここから描く。出典は docs/research/sake-2026-10-10.md と各系譜ページの sources。灘と伏見は1ページにまとめた（slug: sake-nada-fushimi）。GI一覧にある他の産地はメモに素材が無いので行を作っていない
name: Sake

origin.era: Fushimi from the Momoyama period; Miyamizu found late Edo

cells.water: Nada: Miyamizu, hard, almost no iron. Fushimi: moderately hard spring water
cells.conditions: Nada: cold Rokkō wind for winter brewing, Tanba brewers. Fushimi: river port between Kyoto and Osaka
cells.style: Nada: balanced, clean finish, rounder after summer. Kyoto: soft and round, made to sit beside food
cells.gi: Nada Gogō (2018); Fushimi falls under the Kyoto GI (2025)

origin.era: Echigo brewers from the mid-Edo period

cells.conditions: Heavy snow and steady cold; Echigo tōji brewers; a prefectural brewing institute since 1930
cells.style: Tanrei — clean, with few off-flavours. The official text does not say dry

origin.era: Coastal brewing from the late Edo period; Miura's soft-water method, 1898

cells.water: Coast (Mitsu): soft. Saijō: Mount Ryūō groundwater, moderately hard, about 80 mg/L
cells.conditions: Brewers who overcame spoilage with measurement; Japan's first powered rice mill; public brewing research since 1922
cells.style: No GI description. The prefecture links the soft-water method to the birth of ginjō

cells.water: Generally soft, in the brewers' cooperative's words (no measurements given)
cells.conditions: Cold, snowy winters and slow low-temperature fermentation; Sannai tōji; own sake rice since 1988; Kyōkai No. 6 yeast (1930)
cells.style: No GI description. The research centre says Akita Sake Komachi gives few off-flavours and a light finish
